title: Why Ethiopia and Sudan seek to avoid direct conflict despite tension
gist: After drone strikes on Sudanese power stations allegedly launched by the RSF from Ethiopian soil, Ethiopia and Sudan's army closed each other's border consulates, but analysts argue both are too bogged down in internal wars to want a direct military confrontation, even as they back each other's adversaries.

insights.claim: Analysts say Ethiopia and Sudan have strong reasons to avoid a direct military confrontation because both are bogged down in their own internal wars, even as they increasingly back each other's adversaries.
insights.speaker: Mat Nashed
insights.so_what: Expect proxy escalation rather than interstate war in the Horn of Africa.
insights.quote: both governments have strong reasons to avoid opening another front, even as they increasingly back each other’s adversaries

insights.claim: On Nov. 4 Ethiopia closed Sudan's consulate in Assosa, and on Nov. 5 the Sudan Armed Forces retaliated by closing Ethiopia's consulate in Gedaref.
insights.speaker: Mat Nashed
insights.so_what: Tit-for-tat diplomatic steps are a barometer of escalation.

insights.claim: The SAF believes the Rapid Support Forces launched drone strikes on SAF-controlled power stations from Ethiopian soil.
insights.speaker: Mat Nashed
insights.so_what: Cross-border drone basing turns Ethiopia into a party to Sudan's war, raising regional risk.

insights.claim: A barrage of drone strikes hit critical Sudanese power stations under SAF control, including Al-Markhiyat north of Omdurman.
insights.speaker: Mat Nashed
insights.so_what: Infrastructure targeting deepens Sudan's economic collapse.
